name: Airbnb
thesis: Airbnb is an asset-light global travel marketplace whose long-run value compounds through nights growth, ADR, take rate, and strong cash conversion. Q1 2026 growth supports an intact operating thesis, but the stock offers little base-case margin of safety: the revised DCF is about $138 base, $185 bull, and $70 bear. The model assumes 12% near-term growth fading to 4.5%, a 40% terminal operating margin, and 13.5x exit. The key adversarial question is whether fee migration and insurance attach are durable economics or temporary reported-growth support; new money requires either a materially lower price or evidence that nights growth and FCF margin remain strong after those benefits normalize.

tier_1_kpis.name: ADR (average daily rate)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Declines >5% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (mix shift signal)

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs — cash conversion broken. (Universal floor; per-ticker rules below are stricter.)
Operating cash flow declining >10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs.

bear_deltas.note: Owner approved 2026-07-29. The simplified thesis seed captures fee and insurance normalization plus regulatory and host-acquisition pressure. The live workbook uses -5pp/-3pp near/terminal growth and -4pp/-7pp near/terminal margin, producing about $70 per share.

business_model_rules.narrative: Nights & experiences booked YoY < 5% for 2Q — core volume metric stalling; the take-rate compounding thesis fails.
FCF margin < 35% for 2Q — ABNB's structural floor is high-30s; sub-35 means take-rate or fixed-cost leverage is compressing.
Adjusted EBITDA margin < 30% for 2Q — host-supply marketing or compliance costs eroding the structural margin.
